content.title: One workspace for every model, job and metric
content.lead: Develop, test, schedule and govern analytics work in a single hosted place.

illustration.alt: Lattice platform layers: assist, build, run and the engine

content.title: See the platform at work
paragraphs: Follow one change from a question in the editor to a tested model, a scheduled job and a metric served to a dashboard. The tour covers the features most teams turn on during their first week with Lattice.

poster.alt: Video: a ten-minute tour of the integration

cards.title: Ship changes faster
cards.body: A browser editor, a visual canvas and a desktop extension share one project, so each builder works where they are quickest and reviews stay together.

cards.title: Trust every number
cards.body: Tests, contracts and freshness checks run on each build, and failures point straight to the rows and the commit responsible, before anyone opens a broken report.

cards.title: Spend less to run it
cards.body: State-aware jobs rebuild only what changed and reuse the rest, so you pay for useful work instead of refreshing tables nobody touched since the last run.

content.title: Keep the open engine and add what teams need
paragraphs: Projects built with the open engine move to the hosted platform without a rewrite. You keep the same files and commands, and gain hosted jobs, alerts, a catalog and access controls.

media.alt: The release loop: merge, build, check, promote, schedule, notify

content.title: Everything you need to build, run and govern your data
content.body: Each capability works on its own and gets better alongside the others, because they all read from the same project, the same lineage and the same permissions.

cards.title: Editor
cards.body: Write and preview models in the browser with project-aware autocomplete.

cards.title: Canvas
cards.body: Drag sources and joins into place while Lattice writes clean SQL underneath.

cards.title: Orchestration
cards.body: Schedule jobs, run checks on pull requests and promote changes between environments.

cards.title: Observability
cards.body: Track freshness, test results and run times, and route alerts to the right owner.

cards.title: Catalog
cards.body: Find any model or metric with its owner, description, lineage and health status in one search.

cards.title: Metrics
cards.body: Define a metric once and serve the same answer to dashboards, notebooks and agents.

content.title: Give assistants the context they need to answer well
paragraphs: Agents read the same tested models, descriptions and certified metrics your analysts use, so their answers can be traced and checked like any other.

media.alt: Assistant answering a revenue question with SQL on a certified model

content.title: Controls that scale with your company
content.body: Large organizations need more than a fast editor. Lattice adds the access, audit and isolation features that security reviewers ask about, while keeping the day-to-day workflow simple for builders.

cards.title: Single sign-on and roles
cards.body: Connect your identity provider, provision users automatically and decide exactly who can develop, deploy or administer each project and environment.

cards.title: Audit logs
cards.body: Every sign-in, permission change and deployment is recorded and exportable, so reviews and investigations start with facts instead of guesses.

cards.title: Regional hosting options
cards.body: Choose where your metadata lives and connect to supported warehouses over private links that never cross the public internet.

content.eyebrow: What customers say about the platform
content.title: Teams that moved to Lattice and never looked back
content.body: Hear from data leaders who consolidated their tooling on one platform and gave every builder a faster way to ship.

cards.quote: We replaced three scheduling tools and a homegrown catalog with one platform. Planners now open a forecast they can trace back to the plant data it came from, and our engineers spend their time on models instead of glue code. The real surprise was how quickly analysts in other departments began contributing their own models straight from the browser.

cards.line: faster monthly reporting for clinical and finance teams after moving to one governed project

cards.quote: Auditors asked where each regulated figure came from, and for the first time we could simply show them the lineage, the tests and the review history in one place.
